title: IT Manager
description: Job Title: IT Manager Location: This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States. About Us 1mind is building the next generation of revenue teams. We are creating a new category of enterprise software: Autonomous Customer Experience. Our platform deploys Superhumans , go-to-market teammates with a face, a voice, and a GTM brain that serve the buyer across the entire journey with one continuous memory. They engage, demo, onboard, and support in the moments no company could ever staff, so the handoffs disappear and growth stops leaking. Join us as we define the category and build the platform that powers the next generation of revenue teams. When the buyer wins, the company wins. Every1 Wins. About the Role Weâre looking for a hands-on IT Manager to manage 1mindâs internal technology, from laptops and logins to software purchases and vendor contracts. Weâre adding people, tools and compliance requirements fast, and this role makes sure everyone has what they need on day one, every dollar we spend on software is the right call, and we stay secure and continuously audit ready as we scale. This is an individual contributor role, a great fit for a hands-on doer who likes scaling systems and wants real ownership to steward this rocketship to the next level. What Youâll Do Be the go-to for all employee IT needs. Scale and run our help desk with a service mindset, and keep policies, runbooks and the knowledge base current Own the employee IT lifecycle, from devices and day-one access through offboarding. Manage SSO, SCIM provisioning and least-privilege access across our apps, and fix sync issues as they come up Manage hardware inventory and core infrastructure, including our identity provider, Google Workspace, MDM and networking Own every tool from request to retirement. Run evaluations, lead selection in partnership with department leads and stakeholders, negotiate terms with Finance and Legal, then handle deployment, licensing and decommissioning Keep our vendor register and renewal calendar current so nothing auto-renews by surprise. Cut tools that are redundant, underused or overspending, including on AI/LLM usage Partner with the GRC team on SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, GDPR and CCPA/CPRA. Run vendor security assessments and access reviews, enforce controls like MFA, and support audits and incident response What Youâll Bring 5+ years (or equivalent experience) in IT operations, systems administration or IT management, ideally at a fast-growing SaaS or tech company Hands-on experience administering an identity provider (SSO and SCIM across many SaaS apps), Google Workspace and an MDM/endpoint platform A track record of sourcing software, negotiating vendor contracts and managing a SaaS budget Familiarity with SOC 2 and ISO 27001, and comfort supporting audits with clean evidence and documentation Strong organization and a service mindset, with the ability to juggle tickets alongside bigger projects and a bias for automating the fix over closing the same ticket twice Bonus points if youâve used Rippling, SentinelOne, Atlassian, Vanta, or Ramp, if youâve been the first or only IT hire at a startup, or if youâve worked with ISO 42001 or AI governance Why Join Us This is an opportunity to help define a new category at one of the most exciting moments in enterprise AI. Youâll work alongside a team of builders who move quickly, take ownership, and care deeply about solving meaningful problems. If youâre energized by ambiguity, excited to shape whatâs next, and want your work to have an outsized impact, weâd love to meet you! title: Compliance Trust Analyst
description: About the Role Abnormal AI is looking for a Trust Analyst II to join the Compliance Trust team within Abnormal’s Trust organization. The Trust organization is made up of the Compliance Trust and Customer Trust teams. This role sits on the Compliance Trust team, which owns the company’s GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) programs. The Compliance Trust team drives internal and external audit readiness, manages enterprise and third-party risk, and leads governance across information security, AI, and data to deliver a foundation to maintain company's information security, privacy, and AI compliance certifications... This role owns Abnormal's governance and policy program, chairing and running the company's governance committees, including AI Governance, Data Governance, Security Governance, and other governance programs as they are implemented. Additionally this role will hold end-to-end ownership of policy management, from drafting through stakeholder acknowledgment and management of the company’s Policy Center. Governance and policy ownership make up the majority of this role's scope. The remainder of the role will be a key stakeholder in risk management operations, including managing the risk register, performing risk assessments, and risk exception administration. Lastly, this role will also include general compliance support such as audit readiness, control evaluation, and issue remediation. The ideal candidate will have the mindset of an auditor with keen attention to detail, possess exceptional skills in project management, be a good communicator who excels at explaining complex technology to diverse audiences in a way that fosters understanding and ownership, has strong collaboration and business sense, and an adept awareness of our customers' requirements of Abnormal as a leading cybersecurity SaaS provider. Who You Are Proven security experience in an audit or advisory capacity Analytical thinker who exercises good business judgment and resolves ambiguous or judgment call questions without direction Resolves multi-framework or complex audit questions where the path isn't obvious, and designs an approach when standard procedure falls short and brings a recommendation to the table, not just a problem, and knows when to loop in Legal or Security to get it right Confidence and willingness to ask questions, raise issues, and concerns in a timely manner Comfortable owning and running cross-functional governance committees (e.g., AI Governance, Data Governance, Security Governance), setting agendas, driving decisions, and following through on action items without needing to be chased Experienced managing a policy program end to end. Authoring, revising, and defending policy positions to stakeholders, not just administering logistics High attention to detail, process, and organization with strong project management skills to ensure accountability and results Acts as a trusted partner to other Abnormal teams and external auditors on their domain, leading structured discussions grounded in evidence rather than assumption, and represents the function credibly in auditor-facing settings Comfortable interpreting requirements in business context rather than taking a control requirement at face value, and anticipating how upstream changes affect compliance posture Ability to adapt to change, including evolving business and technical environments, and manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment Team player, collaborative work style Self-motivated and able to work efficiently with minimal oversight/direction Owns outcomes rather than activity — accountable for a compliance domain end to end, including audit outcomes and remediation tracking What You Will Do Own and run Abnormal's governance committees  including AI Governance, Data Governance, Security Governance, and any additional governance programs the business needs. Running these committees will include setting agendas, facilitating cross-functional stakeholders, and driving decisions to closure. Hold end-to-end ownership of the policy program, including drafting, revising, and maintaining policies across governance domains, and driving stakeholder review and acknowledgment. Manage the company’s Policy Center which hosts all enterprise policies.Own risk management operations, including the risk register, risk assessments, and administration of risk exceptions, including enforcing the 12-month exception cap with mandatory renewal review and required documentation. Keep abreast of regulatory and industry developments and advise leadership on the potential impact on the program strategy and plans. Ensure program activities align with strategy and manage the timely and high-quality execution of GRC landmarks.
